description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server wrapping Arete streams for AI agent integration; runs as `a4 mcp` inside the a4 CLI

tool_signatures.name: account_status
tool_signatures.description: Show the authenticated agent account, including slug, status, plan, entitlement expiry, claim state, whether trial access is enabled, starter-stack guidance, and the plan

tool_signatures.name: connect
tool_signatures.description:
Open a WebSocket connection to a Arete stack. \
                          Returns a connection_id used by subscribe and query tools.\n\n\
                          AUTH: Prefer omitting `api_key` in agent calls — the \
                          server resolves it automatically from (1) explicit arg, \
                          (2) `ARETE_API_KEY` env var, (3) the a4 login \
                          (`a4 auth signup` / `a4 auth login`). Passing the key as an argument puts it \
                          in the model context and chat transcript, which is \
                          usually not what you want. The response includes a \
                          `key_source` field so you can see which lookup path \
                          produced the credential (never the key itself).

tool_signatures.name: create_claim_link
tool_signatures.description: Create a short-lived ownership link for the authenticated agent. Returns MCP URL elicitation so the link can be handed to a human. The agent must not open or complete the link itself.

tool_signatures.name: describe_sdk
tool_signatures.description:

tool_signatures.name: dev_capture

tool_signatures.name: dev_checkpoint
tool_signatures.description:
Checkpoints of a dev environment: a saved copy of its whole state. \
                          `action: create` (default; `checkpoint` is an optional name) saves \
                          one, `list` lists them (id, name, bytes, created), `delete` removes \
                          `checkpoint` (an id or a name). Restore one with `dev_restore` or \
                          start a new environment from one with `dev_branch`. Plans limit how \
                          many each environment keeps.

tool_signatures.name: dev_delete
tool_signatures.description:
Delete a dev environment with its state and checkpoints. This cannot \
                          be undone: `confirm` must repeat the environment

tool_signatures.name: dev_environment_events
tool_signatures.description:
The lifecycle events of a dev environment, oldest first: created, \
                          woken, slept (with the reason: idle, requested), checkpointed, \
                          branched, restored, rebased, reset, deleted, each with its detail \
                          and time. Pass `next` from the previous answer as `after`.

tool_signatures.name: dev_environments

tool_signatures.name: dev_events

Read what happened in the running `a4 dev up` since a cursor: the same \
                          feed the dev UI shows. Event types: `build.started`, `build.failed` \
                          (with `diagnostics`), `build.succeeded` (with a spec `diff`: steps, \
                          states, transitions, reactions and events added, removed or \
                          changed), `deploy.activated`, `deploy.failed`, `step.prepared`, \
                          `step.submitted`, `step.confirmed`, `step.failed` (with \
                          transactions, signatures, simulation logs and errors), \
                          `instance.transitioned`, `stack.row` (summarised frames of the \
                          protocol stack

tool_signatures.name: dev_follow
tool_signatures.description:
Follow an account in a dev environment: it is refetched from mainnet \
                          every block (an oracle or a pool that should stay live while \
                          everything else stays put). Plans cap how many accounts one \
                          environment follows, and follows count as mainnet reads. \
                          `undo: true` stops following. A pinned account cannot be followed.

tool_signatures.name: dev_fund
tool_signatures.description:
Fund an account in a dev environment. Without `mint`, set its SOL \
                          balance to `sol` (default 100; it sets, it does not add; owner and \
                          data stay). With `mint` and `amount` (base units, a decimal \
                          string), set its token balance of that mint instead (its token \
                          account is created if needed; `token_program` for Token-2022). \
                          `account` is a base58 public key or a dev wallet name of the \
                          project (`default`).

tool_signatures.name: dev_instance
tool_signatures.description: Read one protocol instance of the project

tool_signatures.name: dev_pin
tool_signatures.description:
Pin an account in a dev environment: it is never refreshed from \
                          mainnet and `dev_rebase` leaves it alone, for repeatable tests \
                          (`include_owned`: also the accounts it owns). `undo: true` unpins \
                          it. A followed account cannot be pinned.

tool_signatures.name: dev_preview
tool_signatures.description:
Preview a transaction in a dev environment without committing it: \
                          its error and logs, compute units in total and per instruction, and \
                          every account it touches before and after (decoded where Arete \
                          knows the program). `transaction` is base64.

tool_signatures.name: dev_rebase
tool_signatures.description:
Rebase a dev environment onto mainnet now: every account it never \
                          wrote (and did not pin) is refetched from mainnet, and the clock \
                          moves to mainnet

tool_signatures.name: dev_repro
tool_signatures.description:
Export the minimal state to reproduce one transaction sent in a dev \
                          environment (`arete.devenv-repro/v1`: the transaction, the accounts \
                          it read as they were before it, programs included), to attach to a \
                          bug report or replay elsewhere. With `output`, also writes it to \
                          that file and returns only a summary.

tool_signatures.name: dev_reset
tool_signatures.description:
Reset a dev environment to a fresh fork of mainnet: every account it \
                          wrote, funded or pinned is dropped (checkpoints stay). This cannot \
                          be undone: `confirm` must repeat the environment

tool_signatures.name: dev_reset_account
tool_signatures.description:
Drop one account from a dev environment so the next read refetches it \
                          from mainnet (`include_owned`: also the accounts it owns).

tool_signatures.name: dev_restore
tool_signatures.description:
Restore a checkpoint (id or name) into this dev environment: \
                          everything written since is undone.

tool_signatures.name: dev_scenario
tool_signatures.description:
Run a scenario in a dev environment: an `arete.scenario/v1` document \

                          by path, e.g. a price or a pool

tool_signatures.name: dev_sleep
tool_signatures.description:
Put a dev environment to sleep now: its state is saved and it stops \
                          counting active hours until it is woken. Environments also sleep on \
                          their own when idle.

tool_signatures.name: explore_protocol

                          what `a4 install protocol <ref> --ts` installs.\n\n\
                          By default returns a summary: the release and spec identity, \
                          the deployment the generated client calls (`deploymentId`, \

tool_signatures.name: explore_stacks
tool_signatures.description:
List stacks available in the Arete registry. \
                          Start here: the returned `websocket_url` is what `connect` \
                          takes, and `entities` tells you which `<EntityName>/<view>` \
                          ids to look for.\n\n\
                          NOTE: casing is not uniform across these tools. This endpoint \
                          and `explore_stack_schema` return snake_case \
                          (`websocket_url`, `primary_keys`, `rust_type`); \
                          `explore_stack`, `explore_programs` and `explore_program` \
                          return camelCase (`websocketUrl`, `installName`, \
                          `programSpecHash`). `resolve_artifact` has a camelCase \
                          envelope over a stored payload that may be snake_case inside. \
                          Read the keys you actually get rather than assuming one \
                          convention, and note `a4 explore --json` is camelCase \
                          throughout, so it does not match this tool field-for-field.\n\n\
                          No auth required — public stacks are always listed. If an \
                          api key is resolvable (ARETE_API_KEY or `a4 auth login`), \
                          global stacks are included too.\n\n\
                          Each stack is brief by default: `name`, `description`, \
                          `websocket_url`, `entities`, `visibility`, `serviceClass` and \
                          `websocket_auth.required`. Pass `full: true` for every field \
                          (`http_url`, `subdomain`, full `websocket_auth`/`http_auth`), \
                          or `fields` to choose keys; `explore_stack` reports one \
                          stack

tool_signatures.name: explore_starter_stacks
tool_signatures.description: List explicitly curated `serviceClass=starter` stacks using the existing Arete registry. These are the authenticated stacks eligible for an agent trial. Public stacks remain available regardless of service class; use `explore_stacks` to see them. This tool is read-only and never creates an account or changes trial state.

tool_signatures.name: get_catalog_entry
tool_signatures.description:
Fetch one active catalog entry by kind and slug: exact package \
                          version, the curated knowledge summary, verified SDK targets, \
                          capabilities keyed by stable language-neutral `operationId` \
                          values (e.g. `program/<programId>/raw-instruction/deploy`), and \
                          sanitized delivery state. Use after `search_catalog`; install \
                          the exact version shown with \
                          `a4 install <kind> <slug>@=<version>`.\n\n\
                          The entry is compact by default: identity hashes \
                          (`packageReleaseHash`, `bundleHash`, `setHash`, ...), \
                          `programIds` and release notes are dropped, and a stack gains \
                          `live` (whether it has a hosted stream). Pass `full: true` \
                          to get them (e.g. to confirm the lockfile records the same \
                          `packageReleaseHash`), or `fields` (dotted paths allowed) to \
                          keep only specific keys.

tool_signatures.name: get_entity
tool_signatures.description: Fetch a single entity by key from a subscription

tool_signatures.name: get_program_knowledge
tool_signatures.description:
Fetch curated annotations for one Solana program by slug \
                          (e.g. `meteora-cp-amm`). `section` selects what comes \
                          back:\n\
                          - `summary` (default) — program header, provenance, and counts\n\
                          - `instructions` — per-instruction semantics: what each \
                          instruction does, argument and account meanings, concepts\n\
                          - `accounts` — account-type semantics and field meanings\n\
                          - `surface` — the ingested SDK extension surface for this \
                          program (callable operations with bindings)\n\n\
                          Sections keep responses under the 512 KiB tool-result cap — \
                          fetch only the section you need. Pass a bare slug, not a URL. \
                          Requires an API key (`a4 auth login`).

tool_signatures.name: get_protocol
tool_signatures.description:
Fetch curated knowledge for one protocol by slug (e.g. \
                          `meteora-damm`): description, categories, links, its on-chain \
                          programs with roles (core/periphery/deprecated), related \
                          protocols (composes-with, wraps, graduates-to, ...), the \
                          public stacks streaming its entities, and per-concept coverage \
                          (read/build/subscribe).\n\n\
                          Use after search_knowledge to decide how to integrate a \
                          protocol; follow `programs[].slug` into get_program_knowledge \
                          for instruction-level detail.\n\n\
                          Pass a bare slug, not a URL. Requires an API key \
                          (`a4 auth login`). For callable protocol packages hosted on \
                          Arete, use `explore_protocols`.

tool_signatures.name: search_catalog
tool_signatures.description:
Search the active public Arete catalog for installable programs \
                          and stacks by intent. Start here: every result is a catalog \
                          entry with a verified SDK target, curated knowledge, and \
                          evidenced capabilities (`modes`: build/read/subscribe), the \
                          exact `version` to install, and a sanitized `delivery.health` \
                          (`ready` or `degraded`).\n\n\
                          `query` is free text; `concept`/`category` filter by slug \
                          (see `list_catalog_vocabulary`); `kind`, `mode`, and `target` \
                          narrow to what you can actually use. Without any filter the \
                          tool returns an overview: up to 5 programs and 5 stacks (or \
                          `limit` of each), with `nextCursors.program`/`nextCursors.stack` \
                          to page one kind. Pages hold 10 results unless you pass `limit`; when a \
                          page returns `nextCursor`, pass it back as `cursor` with the \
                          same filters to continue. Drill in with `get_catalog_entry`.\n\n\
                          Results are brief by default: each keeps only `kind`, `slug`, \
                          `name`, `version`, `protocol`, `summary`, `modes`, `sdkTargets` \
                          and `delivery.status`/`delivery.health`, and the links between \
                          stacks and programs (program, stack and protocol slugs often \
                          differ): `programs` on a stack (`[{slug, programId}]`, the \
                          programs it composes), `stacks` on a program (`[{slug, live}]`, \
                          the stacks composing it), `installName` on a program whose \
                          install name differs from its slug, and a page-level \
                          `protocols` listing every stack and program of each result
